screen14-a1.convention_relied_on: three stacked horizontal lines (hamburger) is an established convention for opening the app's navigation menu — my reading, confidence high
screen14-a1.initial_rationale: unlabeled, but the hamburger glyph is a widely-known convention; common-icon exemption applies pending the behavioural test
screen14-a1.deciding_evidence: same control as screen1-a1 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: tapping the hamburger opened the side navigation panel, exactly what the convention promises

screen14-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Return to chat" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen14-a3.initial_rationale: explicit: go back to the chat

test_cases.precondition: reached this page from the side panel while on an empty home chat
test_cases.expected_result: the user is returned to the chat they were in
test_cases.confirms_if: they land somewhere other than their chat
test_cases.overturns_if: they are returned to their chat
test_cases.observed_result: the app opened the 'Chats' list screen, not the chat the user had been on

screen14-a3.deciding_evidence: 'Return to chat' promises going back to a chat, but it lands on the Chats list — the words do not match where it goes
screen14-a3.recommendation: either return to the previous conversation, or relabel it to match where it goes, e.g. 'Go to your chats'
